This report is built on, for each dataset in turn, conducting a permutation-based simulation on that dataset and then aggregating the results.

## What I did

For each dataset, we loaded the intial data used for analysis, and then repeatidly did the following:

  1) Permute the treatment assignment across clusters within block.
  2) Estimate impacts on the dataset with respect to the new randomization.  In this case there should be no treatment effects.  We use the same `compare_methods()` call we use for our empirical data, including the covariate adjustment (we use the "best" option).
  3) Calculate the range of ATE estimates and the ratio of the largest to smallest SE estimate for each outcome for that run.
  
We can then make a series of dot charts, with each dot chart being the set of ranges we found across the outcomes.
We can insert the true empirical data ranges in a random facet of this set of charts to visually see if there are major differences between the true data and the simulated data.


## The datasets missing from this analysis

We didn't run the simulation on all the empirical datasets due to privacy restrictions and computational feasibility.  The datasets dropped are the following:

```{r}
knitr::kable( tibble( `dropped sets` = miss_sets ) )
```




## The ATE ranges and SE ratios

```{r, include=FALSE}

# Pick 14 sim data
set.seed( 4044404 )

n_sim = 16
selected_sims = sample( setdiff( unique( simdat$runID ), "real" ), n_sim-1 )
selected_sims

sub_dat <- simdat %>% 
  filter( runID %in% c( selected_sims, "real" ) )


# Make hidden IDs
sub_dat$blindRunID = factor( sub_dat$runID,
                             levels = sample( unique(sub_dat$runID) ),
                             labels = 1:n_sim )


# Which is the real one??
sub_dat %>% 
  dplyr::select( runID, blindRunID ) %>%
  distinct() 

table( sub_dat$Estimand )
sub_dat <- sub_dat %>%
  filter( Estimand == "overall" )
```


```{r, fig.height=9, fig.width = 9, out.width="100%"}
aterange_plot <- ggplot( sub_dat, aes( rangeATE ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ blindRunID, nrow=4 ) +
  geom_dotplot( method="histodot" ) +
  labs( title = "5 replicates of fingerprint for ATE ranges",
        subtitle = "(true data also present)" ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA))
aterange_plot
ggsave( here::here( "fingerprint_ATE_ranges.pdf" ), width = 8, height = 4 ) 

```

```{r, fig.height=9, fig.width = 9, out.width="100%"}
seratio_plot <- ggplot( sub_dat, aes( ratioSE ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ blindRunID ) +
  geom_dotplot( method="histodot" ) +
  labs( title = "5 replicates of fingerprint for SE ratio",
        subtitle = "(Ratios windsorized at 5x; true data also present)" ) +
  theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) +
   theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA))

seratio_plot
```
